title: 45-Day Identification Strategy
name: 45-Day Identification Strategy
metaTitle: 45-Day Identification Strategy for San Francisco 1031 Exchanges
metaDescription: Building a workable 45-day identification list for San Francisco office and mixed-use exchanges while FiDi and SoMa vacancy keeps values and tenant rosters moving.

sections.html: Forty-five days sounds workable until the clock actually starts, and if you've ever had to source a replacement HVAC unit on a compressed timeline, you know how fast a generous-sounding window shrinks once real logistics enter the picture. In San Francisco, the identification period runs straight through a market where office vacancy in the Financial District and SoMa keeps shifting, which means a building that looked solid on day one can look different by day thirty just from a tenant announcing they're not renewing.

sections.heading: Starting the Clock Before You're Ready Isn't Optional
sections.html:
The 45-day window begins the moment the relinquished property closes, whether or not a short list of replacement candidates is ready to go. Investors who wait until after closing to start seriously looking are working with a shorter runway than they think, since a week or two often disappears before the search even gets organized in earnest.

Building a preliminary candidate list before closing, even a loose one, gives the identification period a running start instead of a cold one.

sections.heading: Why Office Vacancy Makes Timing Tighter Here
sections.html:
A FiDi or SoMa office building can look fully leased on a rent roll pulled in week one and materially different by week five, since tech tenants in particular have been quicker to signal early lease terminations or downsizing plans than in past cycles. That volatility means the identification letter, once filed, is describing a building as of a specific date, and it pays to pull a fresh tenant status check right before filing rather than relying on numbers gathered weeks earlier.

Candidates in steadier submarkets, or asset classes less exposed to tech tenancy, can be worth weighting more heavily precisely because they're less likely to shift underneath the identification list before day 45 arrives.

sections.heading: Keeping Building Operations in View While Shopping
sections.html:
Whoever inherits day-to-day operations on a replacement property, current staff or a new hire, benefits from knowing what they're walking into before the deal closes rather than after. Deferred maintenance, service contract terms, and existing vendor relationships all affect how smooth the first ninety days of ownership will be, and none of that shows up on a standard listing sheet.

Requesting building system records and service history during the identification window, not after closing, turns up problems while there's still time to weigh a candidate against the others on the list. A building with a recently serviced roof and mechanical systems is a genuinely different proposition from one that looks similar on paper but is carrying deferred work nobody has priced yet, and that distinction should shape the ranking before the letter gets filed, not after the keys change hands.

sections.heading: 45-Day Identification Checklist
sections.html:
• preliminary candidate list started before the relinquished sale closes
  • tenant status and rent roll refreshed within days of filing the identification letter
  • building system and service records requested for each serious candidate
  • three-property or 200% rule chosen and tracked against the actual candidate list
  • identification letter filed in writing to the qualified intermediary before day 45

sections.heading: What Filing Late Actually Means
sections.html:
There's no grace period for a late identification letter, and a verbal mention to a broker or an intermediary doesn't count as filing. If day 45 passes without a written, signed identification on file, the exchange fails outright regardless of how close the investor was to naming a property. Given how quickly San Francisco office rosters can shift, building the identification letter a few days early, rather than racing the deadline, leaves room to catch a last-minute tenant change before it's locked in.

Treat the letter the way you'd treat a punch list sign-off before a building handoff: reviewed once, corrected if needed, and filed with a day or two of margin rather than delivered at the last possible hour when there's no time left to fix an error in a name or a legal description.

faqs.q: When does the 45-day identification window actually start?
faqs.a: It starts on the day the relinquished property closes, not when the investor begins actively searching. Building a preliminary candidate list before closing helps avoid losing early days of the window, since those first few days often disappear before a serious search even gets organized.

faqs.q: Why does tenant volatility matter for identification in San Francisco?
faqs.a: Tech tenants have been quicker to signal early lease terminations or downsizing, which can change a FiDi or SoMa building's profile between when it's first shortlisted and when the identification letter is filed.

faqs.q: What counts as a valid identification?
faqs.a: A written, signed identification delivered to the qualified intermediary or another qualifying party before midnight on day 45. A verbal mention or an informal note to a broker does not satisfy the requirement.

faqs.q: Should building system records be requested before identification or after closing?
faqs.a: Before, ideally during the identification window itself. Reviewing service history and deferred maintenance while a property is still one of several candidates helps rank it fairly against the others.

faqs.q: What happens if no property is identified by day 45?
faqs.a: The exchange fails entirely for that transaction, with no extension available for a slow search or a shifting market. This is why starting the candidate list before the relinquished sale closes matters, and why treating the first two weeks after that closing as prime search time, rather than a breather, protects the rest of the window.
